raw_response:
I've been farming these 6 mu in Quzhou for 55 years now. My father farmed this land before me, and I've done wheat-maize double cropping my whole life. I'm 74 years old now, and my body isn't what it used to be—my back aches after a day in the field. My son and daughter-in-law work in a factory over in town, so it's mostly me and my wife doing the daily work. They send some money home every month, which helps, but we're still careful with every yuan. You can't be careless when you only have 6 mu to feed a household.

**Winter wheat:** I'll plant around October 10th, same as I always do. I learned long ago that if you plant too early, the wheat grows too tall before winter and freezes; too late, and it doesn't establish well. I buy improved wheat seed from the supply shop in town—about 25 yuan per mu. It's not the fanciest seed, but it's reliable. I don't save my own seed anymore; the yield drops after a few years.

For fertilizer, I put down compound fertilizer before planting—about half a bag per mu, so around 25 kg. Then in March, when the wheat turns green, I look at the color. If it's yellowish, I topdress with urea, about 15 kg per mu. The extension agent says I should use more nitrogen, maybe 20 kg per mu total, but fertilizer costs money and I have to leave some cash for medicine and emergencies. My neighbor Old Li used about the same as me last year and his wheat did fine—around 400 jin per mu. I'd rather apply a little less than run out of money.

I'll irrigate three times: once right after planting to help it settle before winter, once at green-up in late March, and once at heading in early May. The well water isn't free anymore—they installed meters—so each irrigation costs me. But wheat needs that spring water, especially in dry years.

For weeds in the wheat, I'll spray herbicide once in early spring if the field looks weedy. I don't spray "just in case"—chemicals are expensive.

**Summer maize:** Right after we harvest the wheat in early June, we plant the maize. That window is tight—sometimes only 4 or 5 days between crops. I use hybrid maize seed, about 50 yuan per mu. You have to buy hybrid seed every year; saved seed doesn't work for maize.

At planting, I put down compound fertilizer, about 20 kg per mu. If the summer rains come good, I might topdress with urea once when the maize is at the big trumpet stage, maybe 12 kg per mu. But last August was dry and I regretted not irrigating more, so this year I'm planning to irrigate twice—once right after planting if the soil is dry, and once in August during flowering. Last year I only did once and the yield suffered. I hope to get around 450 kg per mu if the weather cooperates.

For maize pests, I don't spray unless I see armyworms or other bugs with my own eyes. At my age, I walk the field every few days and I know what to look for.

For labor, me and my wife do most of the work—fertilizer spreading, irrigation, walking the fields. But for wheat harvest we hire a combine, and for maize planting in that rush period after wheat, we sometimes hire two young workers for a couple of days. Heavy bags are hard for me at 74. I'd rather spend a little on hired help than hurt myself and be unable to farm at all.
